Generate Publication-Ready Methods, Results, and Assumptions Prose

Source: R/human_interface.R
report_tmle.Rd

Translates a fitted "tmle_fit" object into clean, copy-paste-ready scientific paper paragraphs (style = "paper"), accessible blog/executive prose (style = "plain"), or a complete Markdown report (style = "markdown"). All numbers, learner names, citations, sensitivity E-values, and diagnostic metrics are extracted directly from the fitted object so nothing is hand-typed.

Usage

report_tmle(
  x,
  outcome_label = NULL,
  treatment_label = NULL,
  units = NULL,
  style = c("paper", "plain", "markdown"),
  conf.level = NULL,
  simultaneous = FALSE,
  e_value = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'tmle_report'
as.character(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tmle_report'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted "tmle_fit" object.

outcome_label

Optional human-readable label for the outcome (defaults to the outcome column name).

treatment_label

Optional human-readable label for the treatment (defaults to the treatment column name).

units

Optional unit string for additive outcome contrasts (e.g., "mmHg" or "percentage points").

style

Output framing: "paper" (academic Methods + Results sections), "plain" (accessible blog/stakeholder prose), or "markdown" (combined Markdown document with results table).

conf.level

Confidence level for reported intervals; defaults to the level stored on x (0.95 initially unless updated via retarget()).

simultaneous

Logical; whether to compute simultaneous uniform confidence bands when multiple estimands are present.

e_value

Logical; whether to compute and report VanderWeele-Ding E-values for unmeasured confounding sensitivity (default TRUE).

...

Currently unused.

Value

An object of class "tmle_report" (invisibly printed to stdout) with elements methods, results, assumptions, table, and markdown.

Examples

df <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 150, outcome_type = "binary", seed = 42)
fit <- tmle_spec(y, a, c(age, sex, lab_1, lab_2), estimand = c("ate", "rr")) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 3L) |>
  fit(df)
rep <- report_tmle(fit, outcome_label = "30-day recovery", treatment_label = "therapy")
rep
#> 
#> ── Publication-Ready TMLE Report (paper style) ──
#> 
#> ── Methods 
#> We estimated the causal effect of therapy on 30-day recovery among n =
#> 150 observations (150 observed) adjusting for 4 baseline covariates
#> (age, sex, lab_1, lab_2) using 3-fold cross-fitted Targeted Maximum
#> Likelihood Estimation (CV-TMLE; van der Laan & Rubin, 2006; Zheng &
#> van der Laan, 2011). Initial conditional expectations E[30-day
#> recovery | therapy, W] were fit with a cross-validated Super Learner
#> ensemble combining [glmnet (100%), glm (0%), ranger (0%),
#> glmnet_interact (0%)]. The treatment propensity mechanism g(W) =
#> P(therapy = 1 | W) was estimated with [glmnet (100%), glm (0%), ranger
#> (0%)] and bounded using adaptive sample-size-aware positivity bounds
#> [0.081, 0.919] (Petersen et al., 2012). Outcome measurements were
#> complete across all analyzed observations. Standard errors and 95%
#> confidence intervals were derived from the sample variance of the
#> Efficient Influence Function (EIF). Sensitivity to potential
#> unmeasured confounding was quantified on the risk-ratio scale using
#> VanderWeele-Ding E-values (VanderWeele & Ding, 2017).
#> 
#> ── Results 
#> After confounder adjustment and targeting, therapy shifted 30-day
#> recovery by +0.2245 (probability scale) (across the full study
#> population (ATE); 95% CI [0.0765, 0.3724], p = 0.0029; E-value = 2.42
#> (CI limit = 1.58)); and the relative risk ratio (RR) was 1.88 (88.2%
#> higher risk; 95% CI [1.22, 2.90], p = 0.0040; E-value = 3.17 (CI limit
#> = 1.75)). The targeting calibration step shifted the initial ML
#> plug-in estimate by +0.0253 (fluctuation epsilon = 0.0719) and
#> satisfied the EIF score equation (mean EIF = 1.76e-13).
#> Inverse-propensity weighting reduced maximum covariate standardized
#> mean imbalance from 0.465 to 0.048. Positivity truncation affected
#> 0.0% of observations, with maximum single-observation EIF variance
#> leverage of 4.4%.
#> 
#> ── Causal Assumptions & Diagnostics 
#> 1. **No unmeasured confounding:** Valid causal interpretation assumes
#> all joint causes of therapy and 30-day recovery are captured in W. For
#> the primary estimand (ATE), an unmeasured confounder would need a
#> risk-ratio association of at least 2.42 with both treatment and
#> outcome (beyond measured covariates) to explain away the point
#> estimate.
#> 2. **Positivity (real-world overlap):** Only 0.0% of observations hit
#> bounds [0.081, 0.919] (effective sample sizes: treated = 55.4, control
#> = 85.4).
#> 3. **Consistency & interference:** Each unit's observed outcome
#> matches its potential outcome under the received therapy level without
#> cross-unit spillover.
#> 
#> Tip: Use as.character(report) or style = 'markdown' to copy directly
#> into Quarto/R Markdown.
